condition: the primary outcome (severity-adjusted 90-day mRS responder status) is analyzed under ITT
action: fit a generalized linear model (PROC GENMOD) with treatment as factor and baseline NIHSS strata + thrombolysis use as covariates; test with two-sided Wald chi-square at alpha=0.05

condition: 90-day mRS outcome is missing or collected outside the -14/+30 day window
action: treat as missing and impute via multiple imputation (5 datasets, MAR assumption); run sensitivity analyses (complete case, worst case, outside-window-included)

condition: an interim analysis occurs at 500, 700, 900, or 1100 subjects completing 90-day mRS (or final at 1400)
action: compare the Z statistic to the gamma-family (gamma=-4) boundary for that look: reject H0 (efficacy) if Z >= [2.97,2.86,2.65,2.42,2.02] respectively; reject Ha (futility) if Z <= [0.06,0.13,0.45,1.05,2.02] respectively

condition: prior to the 1st interim analysis, the observed overall favorable-outcome rate is estimated
action: recommend a sample-size increase (>=150 subjects) only if the observed overall rate is 0.31 or higher

condition: severe hypoglycemia (<40 mg/dL) events are compared between treatment arms at study end
action: use Fisher's exact test; additionally, stop the trial for harm at any interim point if the lower limit of the 95% CI for the risk difference exceeds 4%

condition: 90-day death is compared between treatment arms
action: use the log-rank test for survival curves and a Cox PH model adjusting for thrombolysis use, baseline NIHSS, and age; stop for harm at any interim point if the 95% CI for the unadjusted relative risk excludes 1

condition: the NIHSS or BI secondary efficacy outcome is analyzed
action: analyze as a dichotomous outcome via chi-square test at two-sided alpha=0.05; no multiplicity adjustment is applied (only 3 secondary outcomes)
